title: Major cultural elements: language, religion and human race
competency: Discuss language, religion and human race as cultural elements and describe Ethiopia's cultural diversity.

keywords.def: A group of diverse people from different cultures; also called multiculturalism.
A system of communication using speech, written characters, symbols and gestures.
A set of organized beliefs, practices and systems related to the belief in and worship of God or another supernatural being.

en.text: Cultural diversity (multiculturalism) means people of different cultures living together. Ethiopia is multicultural and multi-ethnic, sharing hospitality, respect for elders and patriotism. Most Ethiopian languages are Afro-Asiatic, in four groups: Semitic, Cushitic, Omotic and Nilo-Saharan.

screens.title: Related languages
screens.ask: Amharic, Tigrigna and Guragigna sound related. Which language group are they in?
screens.after: Semitic. Afan Oromo, Afar and Somali are Cushitic; Welaytta is Omotic; Anuak and Berta are Nilo-Saharan.

screens.title: Cultural diversity
paras: Cultural diversity, also called multiculturalism, means diverse people from different cultures.
It can be seen in nationality, language, religion, race, gender, age and ethnicity.
Ethiopians share hospitality, respect for elders, tolerance, patriotism and celebrating together.
They differ in language, religion, wedding and funeral ceremonies, dancing, dress and greeting.

screens.title: Language
paras: Language is a system of communication: speech, writing, symbols and gestures.
It helps us share ideas, thoughts and feelings.
Most Ethiopian languages belong to the Afro-Asiatic family.
table: Afar, Agew, Afan Oromo, Sidama, Somali
Between the southern Rift lakes and the Omo River

ideas.name: Religion, human race and cultural change

en.text: Religion is a set of organized beliefs and practices related to worship of God or a supernatural being; it gives cultural identity and moral values. Human race is a socially constructed category of people with shared physical traits. Culture changes through globalization, the environment, technology and contact with other cultures.

screens.title: New technology
screens.ask: Mobile phones and the internet reached most Ethiopian towns. Did this change how people live and greet?
screens.after: Yes. Technology is one of the factors of cultural change, like cars, computers and the internet.
